A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPS research work. Their text, equations, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching the proof moved from v2's Appendix A into v3's Section 4.

before.justification: V2 reports original ImageNet classification, SQuAD retrieval, and auction simulation results, including additional baseline comparisons in Appendix B.

after.justification: V3 reports original results on the same three tasks, with main comparisons in Figures 1–3 and additional comparisons in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same score substitution, truncated empirical CDF, DKW upper confidence bound, and monotone threshold updates. Compressing the pseudocode does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet classification with ViT, SQuAD document retrieval with DPR, and second-price auctions simulated from empirical bid distributions. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figures 1–3 retain greedy, ACI, and DLR; Figures 4–6 retain ETC and conservative ETC. The new sqrt(t log t) reference curve is a mathematical growth guide, not another evaluated method.

E3.justification: Both retain alpha = 0.9, T = 10000, the same data construction, baseline settings, and three evaluation metrics. Logarithmic regret displays change presentation; the revised repeated-run count is assessed under E5.

E4.justification: No new ablation, robustness test, sensitivity experiment, or case study appears. The added growth guide in Figure 1 illustrates the existing regret analysis without introducing a distinct test.

E5.justification: V2 reports averages across 5 runs without specifying the meaning of its shading. V3 reports averages across 10 runs and explicitly identifies shaded areas as 95% confidence intervals computed from those runs.

E6.justification: Revised aggregates materially change several baseline outcomes across the main and appendix figures. In Figure 2(a), final ACI coverage changes from approximately 0.63 to 0.44, reversing its ordering relative to greedy; ETC undercoverage counts also change substantially in Figure 6. These accompany the reported run-count revision, while SPS retains the lowest-regret and zero-undercoverage findings.

T1.justification: The relocated proof contains local mathematical revisions: Lemma 4.2 replaces inconsistent k−1 indices in v2's Lemma A.2 with k, and the regret derivation changes an intermediate coefficient from K to 2K. Assumptions 2.1–2.3 and the final theorem bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: online conformal prediction under stochastic semi-bandit feedback, high-probability coverage, sublinear regret, and empirical effectiveness on three tasks.

C2.justification: The explanations of feedback-induced bias, DLR's score sensitivity, and the exclusion of discontinuous prediction-set-size losses are retained. The new CDF plateau example elaborates the existing continuity rationale without changing its interpretation or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: Model descriptions, preprocessing details, baseline hyperparameters, and data-source access information are retained. No new implementation instructions, code release, hardware details, or runtime information are supplied.

R1.justification: V3 adds Kleinberg, Slivkins, and Upfal (2008) to support positioning the loss assumptions as standard in bandit research. Other reference changes mainly update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: Most prose and narrative order remain intact. V3 tightens wording, adds a concrete CDF plateau illustration and a brief Impact Statement, updates author information, and moves the existing proof from Appendix A into Section 4.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column conference layout and redraws all six figures. Figures 1 and 4 display logarithmic regret, Figure 1 adds a theoretical growth guide and changes its legend, and uncertainty bands become prominent. Appendix figures move onto a separate page from their explanation.

improvement.justification: V3 makes empirical comparisons easier to assess through explicitly defined 95% confidence intervals over 10 rather than 5 runs and logarithmic plots that expose previously clipped high-regret curves. Local proof revisions also improve consistency. These are useful reporting and exposition gains, while the method, evaluation scope, and principal claims remain unchanged.
